answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists sybils by making each identity costly to build: an agent must lock collateral and earn endorsements over time, like basalt forming layer by layer, while a fake identity is as thin and crumbly as shale - cheap to spawn but worthless without history. An attacker flooding the network with sock-puppets pays the lock-up cost for every clone yet gains no trust, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times more than one honest agent, and the saffron-scarce collateral makes the attack unprofitable before it starts.
